### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

GNOME Terminal.

### Codex doctor report

Relevant sanitized excerpt:

```json
{
  "overallStatus": "fail",
  "codexVersion": "0.153.2",
  "app_server.status": {
    "status": "ok",
    "app-server version": "0.153.2",
    "control socket": "<HOME>/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock",
    "mode": "ephemeral",
    "status_detail": "running"
  },
  "auth.credentials": {
    "status": "ok",
    "auth file": "<HOME>/.codex/auth.json",
    "auth storage mode": "File",
    "stored ChatGPT tokens": "true",
    "stored auth mode": "chatgpt"
  },
  "installation": {
    "status": "ok",
    "install context": "standalone",
    "platform": "linux-x86_64",
    "version": "0.153.2"
  },
  "updates.status": {
    "status": "ok",
    "latest version": "0.153.2",
    "latest version status": "current version is not older"
  }
}
```

For transparency, the same `codex doctor --json` run also reported an unrelated provider reachability failure against a local `127.0.0.1` endpoint that was not available at that moment. That network check was not part of the controlled account-switch A/B reproduction below.

### What issue are you seeing?

The default Codex TUI can continue using stale ChatGPT authentication from the long-running managed app-server after the underlying file-backed auth state in `~/.codex/auth.json` has been changed to another valid ChatGPT account.

A newly started Codex process with `--disable tui_app_server` immediately observes the new account from the same auth file, while the default TUI continues to report and use the previous account.

Quitting and reopening the default TUI does not help because it reconnects to the same managed app-server over:

```text
unix://<HOME>/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock
```

Restarting only the managed app-server fixes the problem immediately, without changing `auth.json` and without logout/login.

This was reproduced with the same CLI/app-server version before and after restart (`0.153.2 -> 0.153.2`), so it does not depend on version skew.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start with ChatGPT Account A authenticated and launch the normal Codex TUI.
2. Run `/status` and confirm Account A is active.
3. Replace/update `~/.codex/auth.json` with valid file-backed authentication for ChatGPT Account B using an external account switcher.
4. Verify that the auth file changed, for example with:

```bash
sha256sum ~/.codex/auth.json
stat ~/.codex/auth.json
```

5. Start Codex without the TUI app-server:

```bash
codex --disable tui_app_server
```

6. Run `/status`.

Observed: Account B is shown correctly.

In the reproduced case this was the Plus account and the current weekly usage/limit matched Account B.

7. Start the normal TUI:

```bash
codex
```

8. Run `/status`.

Observed: Account A is still shown. In the reproduced case this was the Pro account, including Account A's distinct weekly usage and credit balance.

The normal TUI reports that it is connected to:

```text
unix://<HOME>/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock (v0.153.2)
```

9. Exit and reopen the normal TUI.

Observed: it still shows Account A because the same managed app-server remains running.

10. Confirm the managed app-server is also version 0.153.2, then restart only it:

```bash
codex app-server daemon restart
```

11. Verify that the SHA256 of `~/.codex/auth.json` did not change across the daemon restart.

12. Start the normal TUI again and run `/status`.

Observed: it now shows Account B.

Controlled A/B summary:

```text
Before managed app-server restart:
  auth.json                  -> Account B
  --disable tui_app_server   -> Account B
  default TUI                -> Account A
  managed app-server         -> 0.153.2

After:
  codex app-server daemon restart

with auth.json unchanged:
  default TUI                -> Account B
  managed app-server         -> 0.153.2
```

Additional controlled observations:

- The managed app-server PID changed across `codex app-server daemon restart`.
- The app-server version remained `0.153.2` before and after restart.
- The auth file hash remained unchanged across restart.
- A separately running Codex Desktop/private app-server process was not restarted or terminated by the managed daemon restart.
- No `pkill`, `codex logout`, `codex login`, auth-file deletion, or `~/.codex` deletion was used.

### What is the expected behavior?

The managed app-server should have a supported way to reconcile file-backed authentication state after the underlying auth store changes.

Possible acceptable behaviors include:

- safely reloading authentication at an appropriate request/turn boundary;
- detecting that the auth store changed before accepting a new TUI client;
- exposing an official auth/account reload RPC;
- or at minimum warning that the managed app-server is using stale authentication and requires a daemon restart.

A newly opened default TUI should not silently continue presenting and using an account that no longer matches the active file-backed auth state.

### Additional information

The current workaround is:

```bash
codex app-server daemon restart
```

Then reopen the normal TUI.

This report intentionally does not depend on the specific third-party switcher. The important condition is that a valid file-backed `~/.codex/auth.json` changes from Account A to Account B while the managed app-server remains running.

This appears related to broader app-server lifecycle/state-reconciliation issues such as #37893, but this reproduction is specifically about local managed Unix-socket app-server authentication remaining stale after the underlying auth store changes.

When using Luna Reserve after the regular Codex usage allowance has been exhausted, Luna itself continues to work, but file-editing operations are rejected because of the account usage limit.

The important point is that Luna Reserve is not completely blocked.

In the affected session, Luna Reserve can still:

- read files in the workspace
- inspect the project
- run commands
- reason about the requested changes

However, when it attempts to modify a file, the managed file-edit operation / apply_patch is rejected with a message indicating that the account usage limit has been reached.

The Codex App reports messages such as:

"apply_patch itself was rejected due to the Codex usage limit."

and:

This makes Luna Reserve effectively read-only for coding work once the regular Codex allowance is exhausted.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Exhaust the regular Codex usage allowance while Luna Reserve is still available.
2. Start a new Codex App thread directly with Luna Reserve.
3. Open a local project/workspace.
4. Ask Luna to inspect and modify an existing source file.
5. Allow file modification when prompted.
6. Observe that Luna can read files and run commands successfully.
7. Observe that the actual file-edit operation is rejected due to the account usage limit.

I also reproduced the same behavior in a thread that originally used another model and later switched to Luna Reserve.

Most importantly, the issue also reproduces in a brand-new thread started directly with Luna Reserve.

Therefore, this does not appear to be caused by model switching or stale thread state.

### What is the expected behavior?

If Luna Reserve is available and able to continue a Codex task after the regular usage allowance has been exhausted, file-editing operations should also be executable under the Luna Reserve allowance.

At minimum, the same workspace operations that are necessary to complete a normal coding task should remain available, including modifying existing files and creating new files.

If file modification is intentionally excluded from Luna Reserve, the UI and documentation should state this clearly, because the current behavior makes Luna Reserve appear fully usable while silently making coding tasks effectively read-only.

- Workspace file reads work.
- Command execution works.
- File modifications fail.
- The failure explicitly refers to the account / Codex usage limit.
- Granting file modification approval does not resolve it.
- The issue reproduces even in a fresh thread started directly with Luna Reserve.

This suggests that the file-edit path may still be checking the regular Codex usage entitlement instead of the Luna Reserve entitlement.

Related issues:

- #40939 — Codex CLI cannot use Luna Reserve after standard usage limit is exhausted
- #41520 — Cannot use gpt-reserve

Those reports concern Luna Reserve being unavailable more generally. This report is slightly different: Luna Reserve itself remains usable, but file-edit operations specifically are blocked by the regular usage limit.

### What issue are you seeing?

Layering the official ChatGPT Linux RPM on an rpm-ostree system fails in %post:

$ sudo rpm-ostree install /var/home/username/Downloads/chatgpt.x86_64.rpm
...
Running pre scripts... done
Running post scripts... done
error: Running %post for chatgpt: bwrap(/bin/sh): Child process exited with code 1; run `journalctl -t 'rpm-ostree(chatgpt.post)'` for more information

$ journalctl -t 'rpm-ostree(chatgpt.post)'
mkdir: cannot create directory '/var/lib/chatgpt': Read-only file system

Root cause: the %post scriptlet does `mkdir -p /var/lib/chatgpt` (repo/key setup:
GENERATED_SOURCES_FILE='/var/lib/chatgpt/repository.repo',
GENERATED_KEYS_FILE='/var/lib/chatgpt/repository.keys'), but /var is read-only
inside the rpm-ostree bwrap sandbox, so the transaction can never succeed.
rpm-ostree offers no --noscripts escape hatch.

Expected: %post tolerates a read-only /var (skip repo/key provisioning with a
warning), or the repo setup is split out of %post, so the RPM can layer on
Atomic desktops (Bazzite/Silverblue/Kinoite).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Bazzite 43 (Fedora 43 Atomic/Kinoite, rpm-ostree, immutable /usr),
   download the official RPM: chatgpt.x86_64.rpm (26.901.41600-1).
2. Run: sudo rpm-ostree install /var/home/username/Downloads/chatgpt.x86_64.rpm
3. Transaction resolves and checks out, then fails at:
   error: Running %post for chatgpt: bwrap(/bin/sh): Child process exited with code 1
4. Confirm cause: journalctl -t 'rpm-ostree(chatgpt.post)'
   → mkdir: cannot create directory '/var/lib/chatgpt': Read-only file system
   (reproducible on every attempt; also fails identically for local rebuilds —
   the %post always touches /var/lib/chatgpt).

N/A: no session id / token or context-window usage — installer bug, the app
itself never gets installed

### What is the expected behavior?

`rpm-ostree install chatgpt.x86_64.rpm` completes and creates a new deployment
(pending reboot), like any other Fedora RPM. The %post repo/key provisioning
should degrade gracefully when /var is read-only (warn and continue) or be
moved out of %post so layering works on Atomic desktops.

### Additional information

- Related class of issue (immutable-OS packaging assumptions), not a duplicate:

items.body:
## What happens

When `~/.codex/auth.json` is replaced with a different ChatGPT account while Codex is running, the session keeps using the account it started with. `AuthManager::reload_if_account_id_matches` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` skips the reload when the account id differs:

```rust
if new_account_id.as_deref() != Some(expected_account_id) {
    tracing::info!("Skipping auth reload due to account id mismatch...");
    return ReloadOutcome::Skipped;
}
```

The session then runs on the old token until it can no longer be refreshed and ends with "Your access token could not be refreshed because you have since logged out or signed in to another account. Please sign in again."

I understand the guard exists so different parts of the program never see inconsistent auth mid-run, and that makes sense as the default.

## Why it matters

People who use more than one ChatGPT account for Codex (for example to stay within rate limits during long coding sessions) switch accounts from outside Codex by swapping `auth.json`, the same effect as `codex login`. Every running session then has to be quit and resumed for the new account to take effect, which interrupts in-progress turns.

## Proposal

Keep the current behavior as the default, and add an opt-in way for a running session to adopt the new account at a safe point:

- a config flag (for example `auth.follow_auth_file = true`) that makes `reload()` accept a different account id at the next turn boundary, or
- exposing the existing app-server `LoginAccount` request to a running TUI process, so an external tool can ask a session to switch explicitly.

Either would let account switchers cooperate with running sessions instead of restarting them.
